facts.text: The hotel sits on the banks of the Kamogawa River, on a site favored by Japanese nobility since the 17th century, with views of the Higashiyama Mountains.
facts.excerpt: The Ritz-Carlton, Kyoto sits on the banks of the Kamogawa River—a site favored by Japanese nobility since the 17th century—offering sweeping views of the magical Higashiyama Mountains.

facts.text: The Gion and Teramachi districts, known for shopping and entertainment, are within walking distance of the hotel.
facts.excerpt: The Gion and Teramachi districts, known for refined shopping and entertainment, are within walking distance of the hotel.

facts.text: Modern Japanese artwork is displayed throughout the hotel, and check-in is conducted over traditional Japanese tea.
facts.excerpt: This begins upon arrival at the hotel, when check-in is conducted over traditional Japanese tea.

facts.text: The hotel opened in 2014.
facts.excerpt: The hotel made a politely elegant splash when it opened its doors in 2014

facts.text: The hotel is a seven-level structure, two floors of which are sunken to harmonise with Kyoto's low-rise cityscape.
facts.excerpt: the hotel discreetly spans a seven-level structure, two floors of which are sunken (to harmonise with Kyoto’s low-rise cityscape)

facts.text: A waterfall flows from the upper levels of the hotel all the way down to the basement.
facts.excerpt: including a waterfall flowing from the upper levels all the way down to the basement

facts.text: Some suites are Japanese-style rooms with tatami floors, futons and a deep hinoki bathtub.
facts.excerpt: The latter feature tatami floors, plush futons, and deep hinoki bathtub

facts.text: Suite TSUKIMI is a penthouse retreat atop the hotel with views of the Higashiyama Mountains.
facts.excerpt: Perched atop the hotel, Suite TSUKIMI offers a serene penthouse retreat with breathtaking views of the Higashiyama Mountains.

facts.text: Every guest room has a pruned bonsai by the window.
facts.excerpt: center stage by the window, a perfectly pruned bonsai (yes, one in every room)

facts.text: La Locanda serves Italian dishes made from locally sourced ingredients in a setting of wood-paneling with tatami mats.
facts.excerpt: La Locanda, showcases Italian dishes made from locally sourced ingredients in an elegant setting of wood-paneling with tatami mats.

facts.text: The sushi restaurant serves Edomae-style sushi at an 11-meter-long counter decorated with Wajima lacquerware.
facts.excerpt: you can enjoy Edomae-style sushi at the 11-meter-long counter, fully decorated with Wajima lacquerware.

facts.text: Chef Katsuhito Inoue's chef's table is designed for an intimate group of eight guests.
facts.excerpt: Designed for an intimate group of eight

facts.text: The hotel is home to one of the few PIERRE HERMÉ PARIS boutiques in Japan.
facts.excerpt: The resort is also home to one of the few PIERRE HERMÉ PARIS boutiques in all of Japan

facts.text: The hotel has Asia's first LA PRAIRIE SPA hotel spa.
facts.excerpt: Immerse yourself in Asia’s first LA PRAIRIE SPA hotel spa.

facts.text: The wellness area has a heated indoor pool, a steam room and a dry sauna.
facts.excerpt: let your cares fade in the heated indoor 20-meter pool, the steam room, or the dry sauna.

facts.text: Cultural activities include a wagashi (Japanese sweets) workshop with artisans, enjoyed with matcha tea.
facts.excerpt: In this workshop, Japanese sweets artisans will teach you the art of creating your own traditional Japanese confectionery, which you can enjoy with a cup of matcha tea.

facts.text: Guests can learn kenbu sword-dance moves with a real samurai sword in traditional costume.
facts.excerpt: you will learn basic kenbu moves with a real samurai sword and dressed in traditional costume.

facts.text: Children's activities include a Treasure Hunt and Kids Balloon, Origami and Furoshiki workshops.
facts.excerpt: activities such as Treasure Hunt, plus Kids Balloon, Origami, and Furoshiki workshops.

facts.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
facts.excerpt: This hotel does not provide shuttle service.

facts.text: Children under 4 years old are not allowed to use the pool.
facts.excerpt: Children under 4 years old are not allowed to use the pool.

facts.text: Activities vary seasonally.
facts.excerpt: Activities vary seasonally.

facts.text: The pouch given to guests at check-in is made from old kimono textiles and reused wood from Kyoto bridge construction.
facts.excerpt: the pouch given to guests upon check-in, crafted from old kimono textiles and reused wood from Kyoto bridge construction.
